invariants_contrast.statement: A project is a generic named ecosystem spanning repositories or roots; runs resolve project/work-area membership at init and show workers standing safeguards.

consumer.answer: Operators, launch flow, workers, reviewers, and future adapters consume the project/work-area boundary.

payload.answer: The record carries policy, work_areas, and optional defaults.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency configuration resolved at run init, then reflected in prompts and ledger events.

victim.answer: Cross-repo product work is harmed when reuse law stays per-run or per-path and misses existing ecosystem surfaces.

cost.answer: Adds project CRUD, project/work-area resolution, prompt plumbing, and ledger fields.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Keep the single workspace path; rejected because the motivating duplication was ecosystem-scoped.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current orchestrator state stores one workspace path, not project/work-area addressing.

invariants_contrast.statement: Orchestrator project maps to Agent99 workspace; orchestrator work_areas map to Agent99 work areas; current API workspace must be documented/aliased as primary_root.

consumer.answer: Future Agent99 adapters, Brain-facing vocabulary, launch flow, and machine API clients consume this mapping.

payload.answer: Agent99 workspace is the policy boundary, and work area is the named set of roots whose primary root becomes the CLI cwd.

frequency.answer: Read during launch and in every API surface that exposes the path-shaped workspace field.

victim.answer: The future adapter and operator are harmed if a repo path is mistaken for the Agent99 workspace/policy boundary.

cost.answer: Requires stable project/work-area handles, schema wording, a primary_root alias, and compatibility tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Keep calling the repo path workspace; rejected because it preserves the naming collision.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 already defines workspace/work-area architecture; gap: current service launch still takes workspace as a path.

invariants_contrast.statement: Work-area raw records use Agent99's full stored domain, with version behavior mirrored per WorkAreaStore operation: pending->ready bumps 1->2, display-name rename preserves version.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, launcher resolution, future fusion, and work-area CRUD consumers observe the record and version semantics.

payload.answer: The raw value carries name, display_name, primary, additional, executor_id, version, and status.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency work-area declaration, transition, rename, delete, listing, and launch resolution; bounded by configured work areas.

victim.answer: Future Agent99-readable consumers are harmed if lifecycle/provenance transitions expose stale versions or label-only edits look like material changes.

cost.answer: Requires exact domain validation plus per-operation version tests rather than one blanket rule.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Use a simple always-bump or descriptor-only rule; rejected because both contradict pinned Agent99 behavior.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: WorkAreaStore already implements and tests the per-operation behavior.

invariants_contrast.statement: refs/work_area:<name> is stored raw, not enveloped; raw-family concurrency CASes the entire current value, not the domain version.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, future fusion, and any local raw-family writer consume this storage split.

payload.answer: The payload is the top-level Agent99 work-area map; writes compare the whole current stored value.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency work-area CRUD and transition paths; bounded by configured work areas.

victim.answer: The future Agent99 reader is harmed if raw records are enveloped or if a version-token CAS loses label/status/provenance updates.

cost.answer: Requires a separate raw-family path, whole-value CAS discipline, and compatibility tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Use one enveloped JSON store for every family; rejected because Agent99 reads work areas raw.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 already provides raw record storage and whole-value CAS transitions.

invariants_contrast.statement: Raw work-area delete writes Agent99's tombstone {name, deleted: true, version} with positive prior-version-plus-one version, never the generic envelope tombstone.

consumer.answer: Agent99 WorkAreaStore, list filtering, point reads, and future fusion consume this tombstone shape.

payload.answer: The tombstone carries name, deleted true, and a positive version recognized by WorkAreaStore.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency operator delete path; bounded by work-area CRUD actions.

victim.answer: The operator and future adapter are harmed if a deleted work area reads back as malformed instead of unknown/deleted.

cost.answer: Requires reading the prior record before delete, computing version + 1, and testing positive tombstones.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Write the generic envelope tombstone; rejected because Agent99 does not read envelopes for work areas.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: WorkAreaStore already writes and recognizes this tombstone shape.

invariants_contrast.statement: work_area_meta, policy, and run families use the LPC-style revision envelope; raw work areas do not.

consumer.answer: Project store, service, panel, future fusion pump, and future Brain visibility mirror consume this split.

payload.answer: Stored envelope carries revision, value, deleted?; public reads carry exists?, revision, and value.

frequency.answer: Low-frequency project edits plus bounded run status/digest projection writes during runs.

victim.answer: The operator and future Brain are harmed if fusion requires migration or loses projected run visibility.

cost.answer: Adds local KV, revision/CAS semantics, tombstones, serialization discipline, and tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: A plain JSON file is cheaper; rejected because fusion is meant to be a transport swap.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: LPC provides Client and Cas contracts; gap: the orchestrator has no local project KV.

invariants_contrast.statement: Key grammar uses one reserved namespace for our families, while refs/work_area:<name> is Agent99-native and never namespaced; citations and verifier paths must stay inside work-area roots.

consumer.answer: Project store, future fusion pump, verifier, and prompt-driven workers consume key and path-containment rules.

payload.answer: Families include raw work_area, enveloped work_area_meta, policy, run status, and reserved run digest; cited/verifier paths stay inside roots.

frequency.answer: Every project-store key access and every mechanical verifier path/citation check.

victim.answer: The operator is harmed if verifier paths escape granted roots or if future fusion hides work areas from Agent99's fixed reader.

cost.answer: Requires key builders, namespace configuration, root containment checks, and collision tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Ad hoc keys and filesystem paths are cheaper; rejected because they are collision-prone and can escape the work area.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: LPC provides refs helpers for the raw family; gap: project namespace/key grammar is new.

invariants_contrast.statement: Safeguards are versioned policy objects that add required contract fields, not prose-only warnings.

consumer.answer: Prompt builders, worker-output validators, reviewers, and future Agent99 policy surfaces consume these objects.

payload.answer: Each policy carries id, version, enabled, scope, prompt text, contract schema, and mechanical checks.

frequency.answer: Evaluated for every worker call whose worker kind and unit kind match policy scope.

victim.answer: Consuming products and shared packages are harmed when warnings are missed and shared behavior is duplicated locally.

cost.answer: Adds policy serialization, versioning, scope matching, contract merging, UI editing, and fixture coverage.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Plain repo docs or stronger warnings are cheaper; rejected because the motivating incident showed warnings did not prevent duplication.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: Agent99 has versioned capability policy objects; gap: orchestrator contracts are fixed schemas today.

invariants_contrast.statement: Contract extensions are declarative JSON over a closed verifier vocabulary and use the existing repair-retry path; projects cannot inject code or shell.

consumer.answer: Driver, validator, policy authors, workers, and reviewers consume the closed verifier vocabulary.

payload.answer: V1 carries path_exists, citation_exists, dir_listing_matches, non_empty, and enum; failed checks use one repair retry.

frequency.answer: Every in-scope worker output validation; exactly one repair retry on contract violation.

victim.answer: The operator and local machine are harmed if project config can inject code/shell or pass unverifiable reuse claims.

cost.answer: Requires verifier dispatch, schema checks, path containment checks, repair messages, and tests for every verifier.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Arbitrary project plugins are more flexible; rejected because the closed vocabulary prevents code/shell injection.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: orchestrator has repair-retry validation but no project extension registry or verifier vocabulary.

invariants_contrast.statement: Ledger records project_resolved once per run and project_safeguard_seen once per policy id/version shown to workers; amendments win on conflict.

consumer.answer: Reviewers, fixers, seal halves, operators, and future Persona/Brain surfaces consume these events to judge worker knowledge and precedence.

payload.answer: Events carry project/work_area and policy_id/version/text[:300]; run-scoped amendments remain higher-precedence operator intent.

frequency.answer: Once at run init for project resolution and first-seen per safeguard id/version in prompts.

victim.answer: A reviewer or fixer is harmed if a worker is blamed for a safeguard absent from its prompt or if a later run amendment loses precedence.

cost.answer: Adds ledger event types, dedup/re-record logic, prompt integration, and conflict-ordering tests.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Do not ledger prompt exposure; rejected because amendment_seen already makes worker knowledge auditable.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: adopt: amendment_seen already records first-seen prompt exposure; gap: project events are new.

invariants_contrast.statement: Skeletons and slice notes touching reusable surfaces must include cited adopt/gap/reject reuse audits, and reviewers must contrast each decision.

consumer.answer: Planning workers, reviewers, fixers, source repositories, and consuming products consume the audit decisions.

payload.answer: Audit rows enumerate package/source decisions with citations; review rows carry concur/dissent with reviewer citations.

frequency.answer: Planning and review time only; bounded by relevant reuse packages and audit rows.

victim.answer: Consuming products and LPC are harmed when existing shared behavior is duplicated locally.

cost.answer: Adds cross-repo reading, citation work, audit tables, reviewer contrast fields, and semantic review burden.

cheaper_alternative.answer: A stronger warning is cheaper; rejected because the prior prohibition failed.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current prompts require Reuse Posture, not a per-package adopt/gap/reject audit with mechanical slots.

invariants_contrast.statement: Greenfield rule: there are zero existing project records, work areas, policies, or KV entries; no migrations, compat shims, tolerant readers, or deprecation cycles for nonexistent data.

consumer.answer: Reviewers, skeleton drafters, implementers, and fixture authors consume this rule when judging compatibility scope.

payload.answer: Compatibility means matching Agent99's current readers for future fusion while the orchestrator writes the full new domain.

frequency.answer: Applies throughout this pre-milestone design and every implementation/review claim derived from it.

victim.answer: The operator and future implementer are harmed if review/fix work spends scope on migrations or tolerant readers for data that cannot exist.

cost.answer: Costs explicit fail-closed contracts and review discipline; saves migration, deprecation, and legacy-reader machinery.

cheaper_alternative.answer: Add broad compatibility padding; rejected because the milestone is new and the only real compatibility target is Agent99's current reader behavior.

ecosystem_equivalent.answer: gap: current orchestrator stores only the run workspace path and has no project/work-area/policy KV surface.
